Spec-judge round 2 failed builder+architect. Root cause of the two builder findings was one design defect: the listing form claimed to report 'the outcome a run would produce', but pass/fail/no-coverage are findings OF a run and are not statically derivable — contradicting that form's own before-committing-to-a-run purpose. Fixed by splitting run outcomes from projected outcomes (skip/gap/runnable) and drawing a P1-P3 projection sub-graph; the dead 'listing exits 0' edge was replaced with a discriminating companion that forces a projected gap. Also removed a phantom --help flag, and registered conformance/ in the root spec.md placement map (the architect finding).

Adapter-source audit answering whether the GUI-backed backends can only be driven from inside: they are the opposite. wezterm, cmux and otty are GUI apps whose CLIs are clients, so there is no inside to drive them from; the app must already be running and the caller must be elsewhere. Only tmux has an isolation primitive (-L socket); herdr, wezterm, zellij, cmux and otty all drive the operator's one real instance. Inside is never required and is actively harmful for current-relative verbs.

Cold impl-judge on the guard increment returned CHANGE with three findings against the --all real-boundary suite, all one root cause: the test OBSERVED the developer's machine instead of CONSTRUCTING the world the scenario names. Worst instance was a flat bug — conformance-all-exits-zero-when-nothing-bad never invoked --all at all, it passed a bare adapter name. Rebuilt so each test builds a throwaway PATH holding exactly the binaries its scenario names and strips the multiplexer env from the subprocess, making the suite machine-independent and CI-runnable. Rule extracted: a verification must drive its scenario's own When and construct its Given, never assert an implication over ambient state.

Cold spec-judge returned ALIGNED (oracle/builder/architect all PASS) with one content gap: the runner checks the unknown-adapter name BEFORE the inside-a-mux guard, while the CFG drew the guard as gating that sub-graph, and no scenario pinned the intersection. Added conformance-usage-error-outranks-the-refusal plus the U1 edge in the entry-point graph — a mistyped name exits 2 even from inside a multiplexer, because answering the refusal first would send the caller to another terminal to retype the same typo.

Running the rebuilt --all suite immediately exposed two defects that writing it had not: a minimal PATH breaks the npx the runner uses to spawn vitest, and the failing-tmux fixture produced no-coverage rather than fail because a throwing beforeAll makes vitest report its tests PENDING, not failed. Both fixed (PATH keeps /usr/bin and /bin, which is safe because no adapter but tmux installs there; the failing fixture now answers the two beforeAll commands and fails only afterwards). Direct evidence for why written-but-unrun is not verified.

Superseding an earlier follow-up on this shard: --all is no longer verified by unit test only, nor is it unverified in CI. The constructed-world suite is machine-independent, so `pnpm test:integration` verifies --all anywhere, including CI. The spec's 'CI never verifies --all' claim was corrected accordingly.

Clarifying the preceding line, which overstated: machine-independence is a property of the SUITE, not evidence that CI runs it. The suite remains opt-in via test:integration and is not wired into verify, so CI still does not verify --all today — it merely could now, which it could not before. The spec states the opt-in consequence rather than claiming CI coverage.

The spec asserted CI does not run the --all suite. FALSE, and asserted without reading the workflow: pull-request.yml's live-backends job installs tmux and herdr and runs `pnpm cm test:integration`, which now includes it (continue-on-error, so reporting but not blocking). Corrected. Reading the workflow also caught a portability bug the claim was hiding — two worlds symlinked the REAL wezterm binary, which that runner does not have, so they would have failed in CI for a reason unrelated to the contract. Fixed by adding a `present` presence: a gap adapter's binary is never invoked (gap is decided from the suite count before any run), so a stub is faithful and portable.
